page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance provides 8 virtual CPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It features 15.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.88 GB of RAM per core. The hardware configuration includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, operating under the Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6681.49 and a Passmark CPU score of 7237.82. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a Geekbench single-core score of 717.0 and a weak stress-ng single-core rating. Memory bandwidth remains average, reaching 388.0 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 50.08 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Cryptographic operations perform at an average level due to hardware-accelerated AES support, while database operations and static web serving throughput also fall into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3.2xlarge offers a legacy hardware profile with dedicated compute resources and bundled local NVMe storage, though its older architecture limits its performance-per-resource ratio compared to newer generations. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks that benefit from dedicated vCPUs and local SSD storage without requiring high single-core throughput or modern vector extensions like AVX-512.
